text:
Noah: Quick thread: kernel artifact budget is getting out of hand if we let per-layer+shape+band variants proliferate. Proposing a hard cap of N kernel artifacts per model (suggest 24). If exceeded, build system picks prioritized set and others use runtime shims. Thoughts?

Lena: +1 on cap. Need a prioritization heuristic: sensitivity (from calibration), traffic weight, and shape prevalence. Also mark "critical" layers that always get compiled.

Omar: How do we expose this to model authors? They need visibility at upload time. Suggest upload returns a bundle report: compiled_count, shim_count, estimated mem/coldstart impact.

Sasha: For shims, we should define performance expectations. A shim (e.g., linear->packed conversion) will cost X% CPU/GPU overhead. We should approximate that in the report.

Noah: Agreed. Prototype priority order: 1) customer-pin-critical layers 2) sensitivity delta-perplexity 3) traffic weight 4) unique shape frequency. Build chooses top-K.

Lena: Also need a golden-path probe mode: build compiled kernels for top-K and run a short probe in shadow for the shimbed layers to validate quality impact before going live. If significant regressions, hold upload and surface to uploader.

Omar: That implies upload validation infra. We already have light shadow checks for precision profiles; extend to include shim checkpoints. Add opt-in flag `--probe-shims` at upload.

ci-bot: CI note: adding probe-shim will add ~30s to upload pipeline per model. See /infra/notes/probe-shim-costs. :gear:

Sasha: UX question: when runtime falls back to shim at request-time, should we emit realtime event + sample the input for replay? I think yes, for faster ops debugging. But privacy concerns: sample hashes only unless customer allows payloads.

Noah: Emit event including kernel_id, shim_flag, bitwidth, shape, and a request_hash. If customer consents we attach encrypted sample. Default: no payload.

Lena: Telemetry: add counters `shim_use_count`, `shim_quality_penalty_est` (estimate computed from online proxy), and histograms for shim latency.

Omar: For the artifact cap, also consider grouping by ABI compatibility. If two kernels differ only by a flag we can treat them as one artifact with runtime flag. That reduces count.

Sasha: Good point. Document 'artifact canonicalization' rules in build system. Keep the canonical set small: canonical bitwidths ["fp8","int8","int4"], two seq_len buckets [<=1024, >1024], and band id. That gives upper bound = 3 * 2 * bands. With 4 bands that's 24.

Noah: Exactly what I had in mind. Action items:
- Lena: write artifact cap proposal + heuristic (due Mon)
- Omar: add upload report + `--probe-shims` flag in upload tool (PR by next Thu)
- Sasha: telemetry fields + event schema (PR by Wed)
- Noah: draft ops playbook for shim incidents (oncall steps, `ri audit-shims`)

Lena: one more ask: provide a blacklist mechanism so security team can force some layers to never shim (e.g., encryption-related ops).

Omar: We'll add `manifest.forbid_shim = [layer_ids]` and build will honor.

ci-bot: Draft created: /docs/rfc/kernel-artifact-budget.md (auto-link). Build times impacted: +12% on large models.

Sasha: Sounds good. No objections, moving forward.

Noah: thanks all :thumbsup:

Lena: +1

Omar: +1

Sasha: +1
